newsitem.title: JAPAN: Global chip inventory data plan not finalised-EIAJ.
newsitem.headline: Global chip inventory data plan not finalised-EIAJ.

text.p: A plan for global chipmakers to jointly survey semiconductor inventories has yet to be finalised, a spokesman for the Electronics Industry Association of Japan (EIAJ) told Reuters on Tuesday.

The World Semiconductor Conference, a global industry body which groups major chipmakers from Japan, the United States, Europe and South Korea, basically accepted Japan's proposal for concerted investigation of chip inventories at its first annual meeting in Hawaii in April, the spokesman said.
However, specific methods and details of the plan have not been decided, he said.

"We don't even know what the definition of chip inventories should be...we will try to map out details before an annual meeting next year. But depending on future working-level negotiations, the plan could even be scrapped," he said.

On Tuesday, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported that global chipmakers, including NEC Corp, Hitachi Ltd, Samsung Electronics Co Ltd, LG Semicon Co, Motorola Inc, Texas Instruments Inc, Siemens AG and Philips Electronics NV, had agreed to take part in the survey to be conducted on a regular basis.

The investigation is aimed at trimming risks in business management, now under strong influence of unpredictable swings in chip prices, by sharing information on inventories, the financial daily said.
The initial survey is expected to be held as early as summer next year, but plans for such a survey must first be exempted from anti-monopoly regulations, especially in the United States, it said.
